title: Integrated Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Forecasting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition
author: Maya Patel
content:
Purpose
-------
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operating procedures for annual budgeting, rolling forecasting, procurement and contract lifecycle management, and the revenue recognition and billing controls that touch product and commercial teams. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product, and engineering leaders responsible for planning, controls, and execution.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all legal entities and business units within Redwood Inference.
Includes:
- Annual budget process and timeline
- Quarterly and monthly forecasting cadence
- Procurement policy for vendor purchases and approvals
- Contract lifecycle: intake, negotiation, signature, storage, and renewals
- Revenue recognition principles and billing procedures for hosted, dedicated, and private offerings
- Key controls, ownership, and escalation paths

Definitions and key concepts
---------------------------
- OPEX / CAPEX: Expense classification for budgeting and capital planning.
- ARR / MRR: Revenue metrics for subscription and committed capacity contracts.
- Usage Billing: Hosted API per-unit billing (tokens, embeddings) and invoiceable overage.
- Reserved Capacity Billing: Monthly committed fees for Dedicated capacity.
- Private Deployment Licensing: Upfront platform license + support/maintenance.
- RevRec: Revenue recognition in accordance with ASC 606 / adopted local standards.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Finance (FP&A): Owns budgeting/forecasting cadence, consolidation, and financial reporting.
- Legal: Reviews contract terms, IP, data protection, indemnities, and escalates exceptions.
- Procurement: Runs vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and maintains supplier records.
- Sales/Revenue Ops: Submits contracts, SKU definitions, and billing triggers to Finance.
- Product/Engineering: Provides capacity and cost inputs (GPU hours, cloud spend, support FTEs).
- Security/Compliance: Reviews data residency, encryption, and compliance terms for contracts.

Budgeting process (annual)
-------------------------
High-level timeline:
1. July - August: Budget kickoff; templates distributed by FP&A.
2. September - October: Department-level draft budgets submitted.
3. November: Executive review and scenario adjustments.
4. December: Board submission and approval.
5. January: Budget published and target communications.

Budget template and required inputs: (table)
| Line item | Owner | Required detail | Supporting artifact | Approval level |
|-----------|-------|-----------------|---------------------|----------------|
| Headcount | Hiring manager | Role, grade, start date, comp plan | Requisition + Org chart | CFO |
| Cloud & GPU costs | Eng managers | Estimated monthly GPU hours, region | Perf forecasts + vendor quotes | VP Eng + CFO |
| Sales & GTM spend | Sales Ops | Campaigns, SDR quotas, events | Pipeline plan | CRO + CFO |
| R&D projects (capitalizable) | Eng R&D lead | Project scope, deliverables | Project charter | CFO + CTO |

Budget approval thresholds:
- Up to $25k: Department head sign-off.
- $25k - $250k: Head of function + Finance.
- > $250k: Executive committee (CFO + CEO + relevant exec).

Forecasting cadence (rolling forecast)
------------------------------------
- Monthly rolling 12-month forecast maintained by FP&A.
- Inputs due: 5 business days after month close.
- Scenario variants: Base, Upside (+10-20%), Downside (-10-20%).
- Key inputs: actuals, sales bookings, committed Dedicated contracts, churn, usage trends.

Procurement policy and procedures
--------------------------------
Objectives: centralize supplier vetting, negotiate standard terms, and enforce PO-backed spend.

Vendor classification:
- Category A (Strategic, >$250k/year): Full RFP, security review, legal review, exec approval.
- Category B (Medium, $25k- $250k/year): Procurement + legal review, standard SLAs.
- Category C (Low, < $25k/year): Procurement catalog purchase or delegated approval.

Procurement steps (numbered):
1. Requestor submits Procurement Request in ProcureNow portal with business justification and budget code.
2. Procurement assesses supplier classification and performs vendor screening (AML, sanctions, adverse media).
3. For Category A/B, procurement requests security and legal questionnaires (SIG Lite / custom).
4. Procurement sources at least two competitive quotes for Category A/B when possible.
5. PO issued only after finance confirms budget availability.
6. Goods/services acceptance: Requestor confirms receipt in system; Procurement closes PO and routes invoice to AP.

Purchase order template (example):
- PO number: PO-YYYY-XXXXX
- Supplier legal name / tax ID
- Description of goods/services
- Total value, payment terms (Net 30 / Net 45), currency
- Service dates, delivery addresses (if applicable)
- Contact owner and GL account code

Contract lifecycle management
----------------------------
Stages: Intake -> Negotiation -> Signature -> Storage -> Renewal

1) Intake: Sales or Procurement creates a Contract Request in CLM with required metadata: counterparty, SOW, value, term, auto-renew flag, % discount, data-processing requirements, and routing.
2) Legal review: Legal reviews for standard risk areas (IP, liability cap, indemnities, data protection, export controls). Non-standard clauses require Legal escalation and documented negotiation rationale.
3) Commercial signoff: Sales/RevOps and Finance confirm pricing, billing model, and revenue treatment.
4) Signature: Electronic signature via DocuSign (preferred). Counterparty and internal signatories must be recorded.
5) Storage: Final executed agreement uploaded to CLM and indexed (supplier, contract type, renewal date, SOWs).
6) Renewals: Renewals flagged 90/30/14 days; owner must confirm renewal strategy (renew, renegotiate, non-renew).

Standard clause guardrails (bullet list):
- Limitation of liability: standard cap = greater of USD 1,000,000 or 12 months of fees, exceptions require Legal+Finance waiver.
- Data protection: SSAE/SOC 2 or equivalent for data processors; DPA required for customer data processing.
- Export controls: compliance clause mandatory for cross-border SaaS deployments.
- Termination for convenience: allowed for <12 month term; longer terms require exec approval.

Revenue recognition & billing policy summary
------------------------------------------
Principles: Recognize revenue in accordance with ASC 606: identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate to obligations, recognize when (or as) obligations are satisfied.

Common Redwood revenue scenarios:
- Hosted API usage (consumption): Recognize as performance obligation satisfied over time; monthly billing with invoiced usage; estimate variable consideration when material.
- Dedicated (committed capacity): Recognize ratably over contract term for recurring committed fees; any onboarding or non-recurring engineering fees evaluated for capitalization or separate performance obligations.
- Private deployment (license + support): License fees may be recognized at a point in time (if transfer of IP) or over time depending on contract; support recognized ratably.
- Professional services: Recognize based on completion of milestones or percentage of completion with appropriate SOW.

Billing and invoicing process
---------------------------
1. Trigger: Billing events originate from RevOps (contract executed), usage metering, or committed contract schedules.
2. Metering: Consumption data collected per product (tokens, embeddings, seats, GPU hours) and reconciled with system of record by the 3rd business day following period end.
3. Invoice generation: Finance issues invoices within 7 business days after period close (monthly or per contract terms).
4. Payment terms: Standard Net 30 unless otherwise contracted. Large enterprise deals may be Net 45 or milestone-based.
5. Collections: AR aging monitored weekly. Escalation at 30/60/90 days to Sales and Legal for contract remedies.
6. Credit notes and disputes: Documented dispute workflow; credits require Finance approval and a referencing journal entry.

Controls and auditability
------------------------
Key controls:
- Segregation of duties: Contract negotiation vs. signature vs. billing owner separated.
- PO enforcement: No vendor payment without an approved PO (exceptions tracked monthly).
- Access controls: CLM and billing systems access reviewed quarterly.
- Reconciliations: Usage to billing reconciled each period; AR to GL reconciled monthly.
- Retention of evidence: Executed contracts, DPAs, and SOX-relevant approvals retained for 7 years.

KPIs and reporting
------------------
- Budget variance: Actuals vs. budget (monthly).
- Forecast accuracy: MAPE of monthly rolling forecast (target <5% for revenue).
- Days Sales Outstanding (DSO): Target <45 days.
- Contract renewal rate: Target >85% for committed contracts.
- Percentage of spend with PO: Target 100% for >$25k purchases.

Escalation matrix and exceptions process
--------------------------------------
1. Routine exceptions: Department head approves when within delegated thresholds.
2. Policy exceptions: Documented exception request to Finance + Legal; reviewed within 5 business days.
3. High-risk or material exceptions (> $250k, non-standard IP / data clauses): Escalate to CFO + GC for decision.

Appendices
---------
A. Budget submission checklist
- Completed line-item detail for headcount, cloud, and vendors
- Supporting quotes for >$25k spend
- Approval signatures captured in Budget Tracker

B. Sample billing transition checklist for Dedicated -> Hosted migration
1. Confirm remaining committed term and billing schedule.
2. Map SKU equivalence and metering differences.
3. Provide customer migration timeline and invoicing adjustments.
4. Issue proration credit or invoice as required.

C. Template: Contract intake fields
- Counterparty legal name
- Contract value and currency
- Contract start/end date
- Billing model (usage/recurring/license)
- Data processing requirements
- Renewal window and auto-renew flag
- Legal risk level (Low/Medium/High)

Contact and governance
----------------------
- Finance (FP&A): fpna@redwoodai.example.com
- Legal (Commercial): legal-contracts@redwoodai.example.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwoodai.example.com
- RevOps / Billing: billing@redwoodai.example.com

Review cycle
------------
This playbook is reviewed annually by Finance and Legal. Material changes to revenue recognition or procurement thresholds require CFO + GC sign-off.
